question.text: Per SEBI Circular dated December 10, 2021, all registered AIFs must publish an Investor Charter. For NEW schemes, where is the Investor Charter required to be disclosed?

answer.text: On the AIF's Twitter handle and WhatsApp broadcast
In a separate quarterly newsletter only
In the trustee's annual report filed with ROC

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Section 13.5.1, for NEW schemes, the AIF should disclose the Investor Charter in the PPM. For EXISTING schemes, the AIF should disclose the Investor Charter to investors on their registered email ID as a one-time measure. The Charter covers Vision/Mission, business, services, timelines, grievance redressal, and investor responsibilities (see Annexure 13.1). The Trap: Social media / newsletter / ROC filings are not the prescribed channels. PPM for new schemes and email for existing schemes is the mandate. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-A tests Investor Charter at recall. XIX-C requires knowing the 'new vs existing scheme' distinction for disclosure channel. Manager's Pro-Tip: Embed the Investor Charter as a standalone chapter in your PPM table of contents — auditors specifically check for this, and a buried Charter has been flagged as a deficiency in past SEBI inspections.
